en0: Three hundred men. Against an army so big, the Bible says their camels were without number.
And God looked at Gideon's army... and said it was still too many.
For seven years, Midian stripped Israel bare. They came like locusts, ate every harvest, and left God's people hiding in caves.
One young man was threshing wheat down in a winepress, hiding it from the enemy. His name was Gideon.
Gideon was the least in his father's house, from the poorest family in Manasseh. But God doesn't call the ready. He readies the called.
en1: Thirty-two thousand men answered the trumpet. And the Lord said: the people that are with thee are too many.
Twenty-two thousand went home afraid. Ten thousand remained. Still... too many.
At the water, God watched how they drank. Three hundred lapped from their hands, eyes on the horizon. Those were the ones.
That night, Gideon crept to the edge of the enemy camp. And he heard a soldier telling his dream.
Gideon bowed down and worshipped. Then he ran back, and gave every man a trumpet, an empty jar, and a torch hidden inside.
en2: In the middle of the night, three hundred jars shattered at once. Three hundred torches blazed in the dark.
The enemy woke in terror, turned their swords on each other, and fled into the night.
Three hundred men. No plan anyone would choose. Just obedience.
